title: Strumming: How to Practice Counting the Beats | Guitar for Beginners (rhythm counting with 1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and)
summary: This JustinGuitar lesson focuses on building rhythmic accuracy for strumming by counting in 4/4 time and integrating the “and” between the beats. It explains down-strumming on each beat, introduces the concept of up-strums between beats, and emphasizes verbal and physical rhythm training—counting aloud, tapping a foot, and even practicing the motion without a guitar—to develop a consistent, flowing groove. The video frames rhythm work as foundational to the course, with the instructor highlighting the importance of staying “1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and” rather than sloppy, disrupted timing. A future section hints at adding the up-strum as the next step in the technique progression.

sections.title: What is an 'AND'?
sections.description: The speaker defines 'ands' as the subdivision between main beats in a 4-beat bar and shows how to count 1-2-3-4 while the hand moves down on each beat. He introduces the notation of an 'and' as a small plus sign and emphasizes counting evenly across the bar to maintain a steady pulse, setting up the basic framework for rhythm in strumming and the forthcoming up-stroke between down-strokes (the 'and').

sections.title: Counting out loud
sections.description: This section details practicing by saying the counts aloud as '1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and' to internalize the rhythm and achieve a smooth, even flow. The instructor stresses the value of consistency and warns against irregular phrasing such as misaligned 'and' placements. He advocates repeating the cadence with spoken counts while continuing the down-stroke pattern to build fluency in rhythm.

sections.title: How to practice counting the beats
sections.description: The video moves into practical rhythm training techniques: tapping a foot to the beat to reinforce timing, moving the hand in the air through '1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and' without the instrument, and introducing the idea of 'subroutines' in the brain that connect the 1-2-3-4 sequence to the down strum and the 'and' to possible up-strums. The instructor frames these drills as foundational to building a reliable rhythm before adding more complex strumming elements.
